threads_text: Microsoft just offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its workforce, while it plans to spend $190 billion this year mostly on AI. Data center, sales and marketing teams are left out. If your company offered you money to leave right now, would you take it?
caption:
Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its global workforce.
The offer covers staff at vice president level and below on select teams in the US, Canada, India and the UK.
It is the company's second voluntary exit program this year, as it plans $190 billion in mostly AI spending for 2026.

Would you take the money and leave?

paragraphs.text: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, the company said on Monday, October 26, 2026. CBS News, citing Agence France-Presse, reported that the group represents roughly a quarter of Microsoft's global workforce, and AFP estimated that about 27 percent of employees are eligible.

The offer is open to employees in the United States, Canada, India and the United Kingdom who are at vice president level or below, which Yahoo Finance described as level 70 and below. It applies only to select teams. A company spokesperson told Bloomberg News that some groups are not eligible, including employees focused on data centers and those in sales and marketing.

Eligible employees were to be notified by email on Monday, according to CBS News. Microsoft describes the program as available for a limited period, but the reports published on the day of the announcement did not give an end date or the size of the payments. CBS News said the program is meant to give departing workers financial support and career planning resources while allowing the company to lower labor costs.

In a memo to staff, Amy Coleman, Microsoft's executive vice president and chief people officer, wrote that "The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we're evolving our approach to change," Yahoo Finance reported. CBS News said the memo presented the offer as a new choice for employees who may be considering a future outside the company.
A second program in one year

This is Microsoft's second voluntary exit program of 2026. Earlier in the year the company offered a voluntary retirement program to a portion of its United States workforce, which CBS News put at about 7 percent. Those packages ranged from eight to 39 weeks of base pay depending on position and tenure, according to Yahoo Finance.

Regulatory filings show Microsoft had 223,000 employees worldwide at the end of June 2026, down from 228,000 at the end of 2025, CBS News reported. Yahoo Finance said the company plans to spend $190 billion on capital expenditures in 2026, largely for artificial intelligence. Microsoft shares were up about 1 percent in midday trading on the day of the announcement.

The two numbers point in opposite directions by design. Microsoft is spending record sums on data centers and chips while trimming the payroll that sits outside that buildout, and the exclusions make the priority plain: the teams that build and sell AI capacity are not being invited to leave. The 60,000 figure measures eligibility, not departures, so the real effect on head count will depend on how many employees accept.

Microsoft reports quarterly results on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, when analysts expect updates on capital spending and Azure cloud growth. Any comment on how many employees are expected to take the offer, or on a charge to cover it, would show how far the company plans to shrink its workforce while the AI spending continues.
